subject.title: Feature Request: Anthropic Context Management Beta Passthrough

question: Should OpenClaw expose Anthropic context management as a narrow Anthropic compaction/context-editing opt-in, a broad per-model passthrough including provider-defined tools, or defer Memory Tool/provider-defined behavior to ClawHub/plugin seams?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the public config shape, stream/replay semantics, and Memory Tool filesystem security boundary require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Focused core compaction/context editing
options.body: Implement only the provider-native context-management pieces that must round-trip through Anthropic request and stream handling, while leaving Memory Tool filesystem behavior to plugins.

options.title: Broad Anthropic passthrough
options.body: Expose user-supplied beta headers, context-management payloads, and provider-defined tools with explicit compatibility and security docs.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Keep OpenClaw's local compaction and existing memory tools as the supported path until a plugin API gap is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Focused core compaction/context editing
recommendation.body: Implement only the provider-native context-management pieces that must round-trip through Anthropic request and stream handling, while leaving Memory Tool filesystem behavior to plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across recent Anthropic transport/docs work, compaction behavior, and prior review context for the related tracker.
